title: Built a noir storage-auction sim with Claude and FLUX. Looking for honest feedback before jam rating opens. DO NOT RATE.
author: MDawg74
selftext:
Unit 112 is a storage-auction game told in comic pages. Your father leaves you a pawn shop and a letter. Every Saturday you get one look from the doorway of a deadbeat person’s unit, three sweeps of a flashlight, then you bid against regulars who have their own money and their own grudges. Whatever you win, you sell before rent is due. I tried to make a collage of other systems within the game that interact to make the story interesting.

https://reddit.com/link/1xj36fk/video/rfqauey6jiyh1/player

How it got made:

* Claude wrote the code, one HTML file. I directed the design and the story.
* The comic panels came from FLUX.2 klein running on Cloudflare Workers AI. The hard part was keeping the same face across pages. Passing an approved portrait back in as a reference image did most of the work, and I fixed the rest by hand.
* Sound and music are generated in the browser. No samples.

It’s in the Game Gauntlet SIM Jam, and community rating opens Nov 5. Four things I’d like a straight answer on:

1. Does the first auction hook you, or does the story run too long before you get to bid?
2. Do the three flashlight looks feel like a real decision?
3. Do the comic pages hold together, or do they read as generated?
4. I tried to sweep hard for AI garbage, but if there is an in the game, please point it out.

Free, desktop browser: [https://mdawg74.itch.io/unit-112](https://mdawg74.itch.io/unit-112) Please, Do not rate it yet. I want time to develop and improve it. However, I do encourage you to share it around if you like it.
